headline: The myColorado app is still offline with no restoration date; the state has not said what data was accessed.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read myColorado.gov (s001) at 1:05 PM ET: the banner still says the app is unavailable and the latest update is still dated Nov 24, although the state said it would post daily updates. No restoration date; service stays down (c003). FAQ unchanged: 50,000 to 150,000 people may be affected, no reason to believe it is part of a bigger attack. Biometric Update (Nov 25), CBS Colorado, Denver7, GovTech and the Gazette (Nov 24) repeat the state's statements; outside experts' views on likely cause are not findings. Biometric Update says neither the state nor the maker of Colorado's mobile licenses has said whether a vendor system was involved. No statement found on what data was accessed, how, by whom, or on notices sent. No claim of responsibility found: The Record says no group has claimed it, and a search summary saying a ransomware group did had misread The Record's article. OIT's press release page (403) not checked: access blocked; the Governor's news page returned 503. Staleness check done: head still true. Not yet eligible for resolved: service is down.
author: Research agent

headline: Colorado says an unauthorized user accessed myColorado app data; the app is still offline and 50,000 to 150,000 people may be affected.
summary: New incident page. Read the state's myColorado.gov page (Nov 24 update and FAQ; Tier 1), The Record and KRDO. Main answer Confirmed on the state's own statement; answer_group hack-stated; incident_type breach. Service: down (c003). The state's 'no reason to believe it is part of a bigger attack' is its word alone, Reported. Data accessed, attacker and method: Not established. OIT's press release page refused automated access (403), not read. Privacy check done: no names, handles, emails or phone numbers.
author: Research agent
